title: Johnny Depp’s “Ebenezer” Triumphs: Box Office Victory Marks Star’s Studio Comeback – Hollywood Reporter
body:
Johnny Depp’s long‑awaited return to the big screen is off to a strong start, with his new period thriller “Ebenezer” pulling in $6.7 million on its opening Friday—including Thursday night previews—and positioning the film to claim the top spot at the domestic box office for its debut weekend. The modest but solid earnings signal a promising resurgence for the actor, whose career has been marked by a series of high‑profile projects and personal controversies over the past several years.

The film, a darkly comic re‑imagining of the classic Dickensian tale, is being positioned by Paramount Pictures as a “studio comeback vehicle” for Depp, who has not headlined a major studio release since the 2020 biopic “Minamata.” While “Ebenezer” is not expected to match the blockbuster grosses of Depp’s earlier blockbusters like “Pirates of the Caribbean,” its opening performance exceeds the modest expectations set by industry analysts, who had projected a $4‑5 million opening weekend given the mixed buzz surrounding the project.

“Ebenezer” faces competition from two other new releases that opened the same weekend: the low‑budget horror‑thriller “Ghost Soldier” and the comedy‑heist “How to Rob a Bank.” Both films have opened to quieter starts, with “Ghost Soldier” earning roughly $1 million and “How to Rob a Bank” pulling in about $1.5 million on Friday. Their limited marketing pushes and niche appeal have left the field relatively open for a star‑driven vehicle like Depp’s to dominate the box‑office landscape, at least in the short term.

Industry observers note that Depp’s box‑office draw has been a subject of debate since the legal battles that dominated headlines in 2020. While his name still carries considerable weight, the actor’s recent films have struggled to attract mass audiences. “Ebenezer” benefits from a combination of factors: a recognizable lead, a fresh take on a familiar story, and a strategic release date that avoids direct clashes with larger franchise tentpoles. Moreover, Paramount’s decision to lean heavily on Depp’s star power in its promotional campaign—featuring vintage‑style posters and a series of talk‑show appearances—appears to be resonating with both longtime fans and curious newcomers.

Critics have offered a mixed but generally favorable early read on “Ebenezer.” Early screenings praised Depp’s performance, noting his ability to blend sardonic humor with a brooding intensity that suits the film’s gothic tone. However, some reviewers have pointed out that the screenplay, while inventive, occasionally falters under the weight of its own ambition, and that supporting cast members struggle to find footing amid the film’s stylized aesthetic. These critiques suggest that while the film may not achieve critical acclaim on par with Depp’s most celebrated work, it is likely to sustain a respectable run given its opening momentum.

Looking ahead, the weekend’s box‑office trajectory will be crucial for “Ebenezer.” If the film can maintain its lead and see a modest growth in earnings on Saturday and Sunday, it could comfortably secure a $15‑$18 million domestic total, a respectable figure for a mid‑budget drama. Such a performance would not only reinforce Depp’s viability as a bankable star for future studio projects but also provide Paramount with a solid return on a modest investment. The film’s performance could also influence the studio’s willingness to green‑light similar genre‑bending adaptations that rely on star power rather than franchise branding.

In the broader context of Hollywood’s evolving landscape, “Ebenezer” underscores the enduring appeal of recognizable talent in an era increasingly dominated by franchises and streaming releases. As the weekend unfolds, the industry will be watching closely to see whether Johnny Depp’s comeback can translate into sustained box‑office success, potentially reshaping his career trajectory and informing studios’ strategies for leveraging legacy actors in the post‑pandemic market.
